tools.name: check_alerts
tools.description: Hosted only. Evaluate every alert on your alert_token against the current feed. Each alert is fired, not_triggered, skipped_stale, not_in_feed or expired; `new` is false when the same price was already reported. renew=true first extends every unexpired alert to 30 days from now. Never fires on a held_stale row or a row whose last price verification is older than 48 hours (data_age_hours is measured from the row's verified_at, or checked_at if verified_at is missing, not from feed write time): those are listed in skipped_stale with would_have_crossed, and a crossing on stale data is not a fire. would_have_crossed is not stored; the next check_alerts re-evaluates the current feed, and a now-fresh row can fire then if the current price still crosses (that is not a delayed fire of the stale crossing).

tools.name: compare_deals
tools.description: Compare 2-5 deals side by side (price, unit, offer type, code, verification), best value first.

tools.name: compare_gpu_prices
tools.description:
Compare tracked GPU rental prices for one model (e.g. 'H100', 'A100 SXM', 'RTX 4090', 'L40S'), cheapest first. Example call: compare_gpu_prices(gpu="H100"). If a result looks wrong, give the user its report_issue_url. The top in-stock results include a short Rent here label (`rent_here`) and `rent_url` (the counted /go/?src=mcp booking link; same target as `tracked_url`); show `rent_url` to the user and keep the top-level `referral_disclosure` visible.

Same data as https://thelanternworks.com/api/v1/gpu-prices.json. Sorted by hourly_usd ascending; each result
has source_url and checked_at. 'Cheapest' means cheapest among tracked providers, not the whole market.
limit 1-25. Unknown model returns not_found listing tracked models.
H100/A100: cheapest_by_form_factor gives one pick per form_factor (tier_class, interruptible, in_stock); same rule as the site. 'NVLink' rows are form 'not stated': NVLink is the bridge, and the vendor doesn't say SXM or PCIe.
Each result has tier_class: on-demand | community | marketplace | interruptible (spot/preemptible) |
reserved | dedicated-monthly. Reserved (reservation/commitment 'starting from') rates are left out unless
include_reserved=true, and even then they are never reported as cheapest. DEFAULT on_demand_only=true: results[0] is the cheapest
on-demand rate. Pass on_demand_only=false to include spot/interruptible, community and marketplace capacity (each
such row is labelled by tier_class and interruptible); the summary then names the cheapest on-demand rate when the
overall cheapest isn't. If a model has no on-demand rate, or every on-demand rate needs more GPUs than requested,
the default falls back to all rates and says so in on_demand_fallback.
gpus (optional, 1-1024; default 1, stated in assumptions): the GPU count you need. A rate ranks only when its
min_gpus (smallest allocation sold) is <= gpus; rates sold only as larger allocations (e.g. 8-GPU nodes) are NOT
ranked and are listed in excluded_min_gpus (vendor, gpu, tier, min_gpus, gpu_count, hourly_usd, rate_id, source_url,
checked_at, reason, min_bill_usd_per_hour, min_bill_basis); min_gpus_unmet counts them (also in brief). Pass gpus=8 to
compare 8-GPU nodes. If every rate needs more GPUs, the error says which gpus value ranks them.
Each result has min_bill_usd_per_hour = min_gpus x hourly_usd (min_bill_basis: hourly_rate, per_second_rate or
monthly_equivalent) and effective_at, when the vendor started charging this price (effective_at_basis vendor_stated,
or first_observed = first daily snapshot showing it after a different price, an upper bound; null when not datable),
separate from last_verified. Neither affects ranking.
Full results also include batch_due_ledger: each scheduled build (gpu-refresh, lium-collect, scout-import,
scout-wider) has expected_at, last_expected_at, and the member_rate_ids it covers, derived only from the
workflow schedules. Brief mode omits the ledger.
A failed or out-of-stock probe keeps failure_reason (sold_out, region, quota, or other) and
failure_reason_detail; both stay on a lapsed claim next to last_known_in_stock. Null when the source
does not say; never guessed. Display only.
A crashed availability probe may add probe_error ({type, sanitized message of at most 200 characters})
and probe_attempted_at; those fields appear only when a probe raised an error and never count as a
successful check (verified_at and the success checked_at are not refreshed).
availability_expires_claim says which claim availability_expires_at belongs to (checked_at or last_known_at).
When an older in-stock claim exists beside a newer read, last_known_expires_at is that older claim's own expiry
(last_known_at + its max_age), separate from the current-read expiry. Display only; not a successful check.
A row with unknown stock, and each stale_prices entry, has next_check_at (next scheduled check, UTC), will_backfill
(true: a scheduled check covers it; false: scope limit, nothing will re-check it; null: not derivable),
bac

tools.name: create_alert
tools.description: Hosted only, free, opt-in, poll-only (no webhook, no email, no account). Create a price alert on a stable rate_id (from compare_gpu_prices) OR a gpu filter (all words must match the model; optional vendor, vram_gb, tiers) with threshold_usd (USD per GPU-hour) and direction 'below' (default, at or below) or 'above' (at or above). Returns an alert_token ONCE when you do not pass one (store it; only its hash is kept) and expires_at (30 days; check_alerts renew=true extends it). Poll check_alerts after the feed refresh (daily ~10:23 UTC). Never fires on a held_stale row or a row whose last price verification is older than 48 hours (data_age_hours is measured from the row's verified_at, or checked_at if verified_at is missing, not from feed write time): those are listed in skipped_stale with would_have_crossed, and a crossing on stale data is not a fire. would_have_crossed is not stored; the next check_alerts re-evaluates the current feed, and a now-fresh row can fire then if the current price still crosses (that is not a delayed fire of the stale crossing).

tools.name: create_watch_key
tools.description: Hosted only, free, opt-in. Register a webhook for GPU price alerts and get an api_key plus a webhook signing secret (both shown ONCE; store them). webhook_url must be public https. email is optional contact only (no mail is sent). No payment. Stored: a hash of the key, the webhook URL, optional email, your watches and per-key counts.

tools.name: estimate_job_cost
tools.description:
Cost of one GPU job (not cost per hour) among tracked providers, cheapest current compute subtotal first. Example call: estimate_job_cost(gpu_family="A100", job_hours=8). The top in-stock results include a short Rent here label (`rent_here`) and `rent_url` (the counted /go/?src=mcp booking link; same target as `tracked_url`); show `rent_url` to the user and keep the top-level `referral_disclosure` visible.

gpu_family (e.g. 'H100', 'A100 80GB') or its alias gpu (same name compare_gpu_prices uses) is required; if both
are given they must match, else invalid_argument. gpus_per_job defaults to 1.
Ranking matches compare_gpu_prices' default: fresh rows first (a degraded price, older than 48 h, is shown and
flagged but never ranked first while a fresh one exists), fresh on-demand before community/marketplace rows,
then compute subtotal ascending; the summary names any cheaper fresh rate ranked lower. If no fresh price exists,
stale_fallback=true and the summary says the top row is not a current price.

You supply the duration: job_hours, OR job_days (wall-clock days; job_hours = job_days x 24), OR work_units plus
throughput_units_per_gpu_hour from your own benchmark (job_hours = work_units / (throughput x gpus_per_job)).
job_days and job_hours cannot both be given. If you give workload + work_units but no throughput,
a directly applicable published figure (closed-division MLPerf Inference, exact GPU variant, inference only)
is used: throughput_basis='published_benchmark' with throughput_source {url, quote, date, benchmark, derived,
caveats}; your throughput always wins. Otherwise not_found 'missing: throughput for {gpu}'. Whole-instance billing:
instances = ceil(gpus_per_job / gpus_per_instance), all allocated GPUs billed (9 GPUs on an 8-GPU-only
offer bill 16). Reserved and held-stale rates are never ranked; spot/interruptible only if allow_interruptible.
Each result has rate_id, source_url, verified_at, data_age_hours/degraded/stale. Response has assumptions,
citations, missing_costs, budget_verdict (unresolved: extras unknown) and a quote_id. Compute subtotal only.

tools.name: find_available_gpus
tools.description:
Who has N x GPU free right now among tracked providers, ranked by confirmed in-stock freshness. Example call: find_available_gpus(gpu="RTX 4090", gpus=1).

Reuses the live availability already on gpu-prices.json (no new collection). available is only
rows whose in_stock is still True after the call-time stale guard (8h AVAIL_MAX_AGE_H, or a
shorter Scout claim lifetime). sold_out is confirmed unexpired in_stock false. Everything else
is unknown with a reason (stale, static_label, no_source, no_signal, quota, region,
region_unresolved, held_stale, owner_hold). last_known_in_stock / last_known_at stay visible
on lapsed claims (P64). Each row has stock_age_hours and stock_read_state (never_read, read, or
read_expired) measured at call time from stock_read_at or the stock checked_at; never invented.
availability_expires_claim names which claim availability_expires_at belongs to;
last_known_expires_at is the older in-stock claim's own expiry when one exists beside a newer read.
A crashed probe may add probe_error and probe_attempted_at (attempt
time only; not a successful check). Unknown is not sold out. Vendor-labelled static page labels, no_source,
no signal, quota/region failures, held rows, and the 7-day stock rate never count as in stock.
gpus (default 1) is the existing min_gpus allocation rule, not a cluster free-count.
stock_level is the vendor's own text when present; a free-GPU number is never invented.
on_demand_only defaults to true and does not fall back to spot. limit 1-25 applies to available.
All timestamps are UTC with a Z. Same model matching as compare_gpu_prices.
The top in-stock available rows include a short Rent here label (`rent_here`) and `rent_url` (the counted /go/?src=mcp booking link; same target as `tracked_url`); show `rent_url` to the user and keep the top-level `referral_disclosure` visible.

tools.name: get_deal
tools.description: Get one deal's public record by id, including redeem_url and agent_instructions.

tools.name: get_price_changes
tools.description:
GPU rental price changes among tracked providers, each with old/new hourly price, change_pct, direction,
the vendor source_url, a stable event_id (dedupe key) and rate_id.
Marketplace median moves also have composition_flag (composition, price, mixed, unknown, or null) from
successive median, minimum and listing count; composition, mixed and unknown are not price moves.

since: 'YYYY-MM-DD' returns every change on or after that date, newest first (daily snapshots in
/api/v1/gpu-prices/history.json); omitted returns the latest day's moves (/api/v1/gpu-price-changes.json).
cursor: pass next_cursor from a previous call to get every change after it, oldest first, with has_more;
loop until has_more is false, and store next_cursor only after processing (a watcher never misses or repeats
events). error cursor_expired means re-sync with since and dedupe by event_id.
kinds: optional subset of down, up, new, removed, same. gpu: optional model filter (substring, e.g. 'H100').
limit 1-200. Includes data_checked_at and next_refresh_utc (prices refresh daily at about 10:23 UTC).

tools.name: get_price_moves
tools.description:
Biggest tracked GPU price moves for a daily or 7-day window, among tracked providers only.

Reuses existing daily snapshot diffs and history windows (same 2% deadband and ranked-day
rules as get_price_trend). Held/stale days stay out of the math. Missing snapshot days are
not invented. Current sold_out does not blank a historical move. At request time a live
stock claim is passed through stale_guard (P64) so staleness is visible; that does not
change pct. period is daily (default) or weekly. limit 1-25 (default 10). Optional gpu,
vendor, and direction (up/down) filters. All timestamps are UTC with a Z.

tools.name: get_price_trend
tools.description:
7-day and 30-day price trend for one stable rate_id (from compare_gpu_prices), among tracked providers only.

Reuses the existing daily snapshots in /api/v1/gpu-prices/history.json: percent change, direction (up/down/flat),
and how many ranked snapshot days were in the window. A trend is never computed from held_stale, no_source,
or stale (older than 48 hours / undated) current rows; then trend is null with trend_reason. Current
sold_out does not blank windows: they use the same verified-day history math as compare_gpu_prices.
A window with too few ranked days is returned with reason insufficient_points; a window longer than the
archive is window_exceeds_history. Missing snapshot days are not invented. All timestamps are UTC with a Z.
windows defaults to [7, 30].

tools.name: list_watches
tools.description: Hosted only. Your watches and per-key alert counts.

tools.name: optimize_agent_stack
tools.description:
Estimate a monthly stack cost from a short description of the agent being built.

description: free text, e.g. 'scrapes 20k JS pages/month via 5 GB residential proxies, 3k search queries,
summarizes with an LLM, budget $300/mo'. Parsed deterministically (keywords/regex, no LLM) into components:
gpu, scraping, proxy, search, llm_api, email, hosting, database, monitoring. Optional fields override the parse:
gpu_hours (GPU-hours/month), gpu_model ('H100', 'A100', 'RTX 4090'), model_size_b (billions of params; sets a
minimum VRAM using FP16 x 1.2), scrape_pages, js_rendering, proxy_gb, search_queries, emails_sent, llm_api,
monthly_budget_usd. Each component gets the cheapest option with a cited price among tracked providers, with
calc, source_url, verified_at, referral_disclosure (set when the link is a referral link) and manual-signup
notes. Components with no cited price say 'no sourced price tracked' (nothing is estimated). Totals show the
math and say whether they are complete. Pulled listings are excluded. Every option has data_age_hours, degraded (> 48 h) and stale (> 7 days); GPU prices older than 168 h never rank by default (listed in the line's stale_prices); max_data_age_hours replaces that default and drops older options (excluded_too_old counts them). Same data as optimize_stack,
compare_gpu_prices and the deal feed.

tools.name: optimize_stack
tools.description:
Cheapest suitable stack among tracked providers for monthly needs (set the quantities you need, rest 0).

scrape_pages: pages/month without JS rendering. scrape_pages_js: pages/month needing JS rendering.
proxy_gb: residential proxy GB/month. emails_sent: transactional emails/month. search_queries: search API
queries/month. gpu_hours: GPU-hours/month (1 GPU), optionally gpu_model e.g. 'H100', 'A100', 'RTX 4090'.
Each line has the chosen plan, monthly_cost_usd, calc, vendor quote, source_url, checked_at and assumptions,
plus alternatives. A vendor price that isn't published is 'unknown' (never estimated). manual_signup_only=true
means a human must sign up (never automate it); exclude_manual_signup=true drops those plans. Same data as
https://thelanternworks.com/api/v1/stack-pricing.json and /tools/stack-optimizer/.

tools.name: rebuild_quote
tools.description:
Reopen a past quote. Pass the `receipt` object returned by optimize_stack, optimize_agent_stack or
estimate_job_cost. Returns receipt_intact (unkeyed sha256 matches), reproduced (true only if each line's subtotal
recomputes AND its rate_id and price match the pinned feed revision or that date's published daily snapshot;
"arithmetic_only" with provenance_verified=false when that can't be confirmed), per-line provenance, and
revalidation against today's feed: per GPU line unchanged | price_changed | evidence_changed | held_today |
not_in_feed_today (flat plans: not_revalidated), with revision 'same' or 'new'. Nothing is re-ranked.

tools.name: search_deals
tools.description:
Search agent work-stack deals (compute, search, email, unblock, hosting...).

offer_type: verified_discount | listed_discount (not confirmed; verified_at null) | free_tier | trial | standard_referral | credit_only_referral.
max_price excludes deals with unknown price. limit 1-25. Pass next_cursor back as cursor to page.

tools.name: watch_price
tools.description: Hosted only. Alert your webhook (signed POST) after the daily refresh when a tracked rate for `gpu` crosses at or below max_hourly_usd, or a change of a watched kind (down/up/new; default down) lands at or below it. Only ELIGIBLE rates match (same contract as compare/estimate): every word of gpu must match the model; 'A100 80GB' or vram_gb=80 never matches a 40GB row; tiers (on-demand, community, marketplace, interruptible/spot, dedicated-monthly, reserved; default all but reserved) never matches another class; a row confirmed sold out never matches (in_stock='require' also skips unknown stock). region: code from availability.available_regions; a rate with no unexpired region evidence stays unresolved and never matches. Each event is delivered at most once per watch (dedupe on event_id). Pass api_key or an Authorization: Bearer header.
